caption: My pension was calculated for one person. I'm feeding three. Any other grandparents doing the sums like this?

slides.title:
How I live on
my R14 500
p/m pension
Living in Graaff-Reinet
slides.body:
Female, 68
Widowed, two grandchildren live with her
Income: Government pension & late husband's annuity
Net income: R14 500 p/m

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Feeding three of us, growing boys eat like men now
slides.body: My pension was calculated for one person. Life had other plans.

slides.title: Grandchildren's school costs
slides.includes: Uniforms, stationery, the school trip nobody warns you about
slides.body: Their mother, my daughter, works in Cape Town and sends what she can. It isn't always enough.

slides.title: Medical aid top-up & medication
slides.includes: My blood pressure tablets, my hip, the boys' check-ups
slides.body: This is the one that only ever goes up.

slides.title: Electricity & water
slides.includes: Prepaid electricity, municipal water and rates
slides.body: Karoo winters are longer than people think.

slides.title: Funeral policy
slides.includes: Cover for all three of us now, increased after my husband passed
slides.body: I paid his out in full. I'm not leaving that burden on anyone else.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Cellphone, transport to the clinic, church, the stokvel I've kept since 1994, a little pocket money for the boys
slides.body: The stokvel is the one thing I refuse to give up, pension or not.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R14 500 for three of us. It works, most months, because it has to.

slides.title: I wanted to know I wasn't overspending on them
slides.body:
I uploaded my pension statements to Beyond Horizon once the boys moved in, just to see the real picture.

It turns out I wasn't overspending — I was supporting more people on the same pension.

No bank login needed.
